summary: This lecture continues the study of Zadul-Ma'ad (Provisions for the Hereafter) by Ibn al-Qayyim, focusing on etiquettes of speech and the early history of Islam. The first portion covers proper Islamic etiquettes in teaching and disseminating knowledge, distinguishing between explicit divine rulings and scholarly opinions, and addressing prohibited speech such as disclosing marital intimacy, spreading unverified claims, and excessive self-glorification. The lecture emphasizes the importance of vetting information before repeating it and warns against arrogance through Quranic examples. The second portion transitions into the biography section of Zadul-Ma'ad, discussing the stages of Islamic dawah (preaching) and the earliest Muslims, including Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, Khadijah, Ali, Zaid ibn Harithah, and others. Special attention is given to Zaid ibn Harithah's story—his adoption by the Prophet and how his name was eventually changed by divine revelation, becoming the only companion explicitly mentioned by name in the Quran.
